title: eval-harness: add prompt-set regression CI hook and quality gating for prompt drift
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Stopped occasional prompt-set regressions slipping into main because eval runs were noisy and not enforced in CI. This PR adds a CI hook that runs a fast prompt-set regression suite on changed prompts and model outputs to block merges when quality drops exceed configurable thresholds.

What it does: 1) Introduces eval-harness/ci/prompt_regression_check.py, a lightweight runner that downloads the baseline oracle for the active prompt-set, runs model outputs in a headless mode, computes configured metrics (BLEU, EM, and a Redwood-specific similarity metric), and compares deltas against gating thresholds. 2) Adds a GitHub Actions job (eval-prompt-regression) that triggers on PRs touching prompting/eval assets or the eval harness code. 3) Exposes gating configuration via .github/eval-gating.yaml and supports per-repo overrides. 4) Integrates with existing CI status reporting and sets an explicit "quality-gate" check.

Checklist: - [x] Core runner implemented and unit-tested - [x] GH Actions workflow wired and smoke-tested - [x] Config format documented in eval-harness/README.md - [x] Threshold defaults chosen after calibration runs (see ENG-1423) - [x] Added telemetry tracing hooks for later dashboarding

Deployment notes: The job is enabled for the redwood repo and for the eval-harness subproject. Thresholds are conservative by default and can be tuned via Linear ENG-1423. For Dedicated/private deployments customers can opt-in to run the same checks in their pipelines.

Backward compatibility: Non-breaking; if a repo has no eval-gating config the check is skipped.

References: Linear ENG-1423, design notes in docs/eval-harness/quality-gating.md.

release_notes: Add CI prompt-set regression check and configurable quality gating. New GH Actions job 'eval-prompt-regression' will block merges when metric deltas exceed thresholds. Defaults are conservative; see docs/eval-harness/quality-gating.md for tuning.
notes_for_reviewers: Key places to review: thresholding logic in prompt_regression_check.py, the GH Actions workflow triggers, and the docs/config examples. The runner is intentionally synchronous and lightweight to keep CI runtime under configurable limits. Performance calibration results are included in benchmarks/ci/calibration/.
